/-!
# Erdős Problem 664

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/664](https://www.erdosproblems.com/664)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., _On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved_.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, _Some unsolved problems_. Combinatorics, geometry and probability
  (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real Finset

namespace Erdos664

/--
Let $c<1$ be some constant and $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ be such that
$\lvert A_i\rvert >c\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$ and $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for all $i\neq j$.

Must there exist some set $B$ such that $B\cap A_i\neq \emptyset$ and
$\lvert B\cap A_i\rvert \ll_c 1$ for all $i$?

The answer is no, proved by Alon: if $q$ is a large prime power and $n=m=q^2+q+1$ then there
exist $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that
$\lvert A_i\rvert \geq \tfrac{2}{5}\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$ and $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for
all $i\neq j$, and yet if $B$ has non-empty intersection with all $A_i$ then there exists $A_j$
such that $\lvert B\cap A_j\rvert \gg \log n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos664.lean#L214"]
theorem erdos_664 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 → ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ i, c * √n < (A i).card) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).card ≤ 1) →
        ∃ B : Finset (Fin n), (∀ i, (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧
          ∀ i, (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K := by
  sorry

/-- Alon's counterexample already works for $c=2/5$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos664.lean#L214"]
theorem erdos_664.variants.two_fifths :
    ¬ ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ i, 2 / 5 * √n < (A i).card) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).card ≤ 1) →
        ∃ B : Finset (Fin n), (∀ i, (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧
          ∀ i, (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K := by
  sorry

/--
In [Er81] the condition $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for all $i\neq j$ is replaced by every
two points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ being contained in exactly one $A_i$, that is,
$A_1,\ldots,A_m$ is a pairwise balanced block design (and the condition $c<1$ is omitted). This
weaker version remains open, although Alon conjectures the answer there to also be no.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_664.variants.block_design : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ x y : Fin n, x ≠ y → ∃! i, x ∈ A i ∧ y ∈ A i) →
        ∃ B : Finset (Fin n), (∀ i, (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧
          ∀ i, (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K := by
  sorry

end Erdos664

findings.description: Lines 77–80 omit the block-size hypothesis |A_i| > c√n and the parameter c on which K may depend. The Lean instead asks for one absolute K for every family satisfying only unique pair coverage. Its right-hand side is trivially false: take n = m = 1 and A 0 = ∅. There are no distinct points, so the hypothesis holds, but no B can meet the empty block. The exact negation of this right-hand side was proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Merely excluding empty blocks would not fix the omission: two disjoint r-point blocks together with all cross-pairs form a pairwise balanced design, and any transversal contains an entire r-point block, requiring K ≥ r.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős [Er81], §VI, first block-design problem (p. 12 of https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf), asks whether 'to every c₁ there is a c₂' such that a pairwise balanced block design 'satisfying |A_i| > c₁ n^(1/2)' admits Q with 1 ≤ |Q ∩ A_i| ≤ c₂. Alon's Blocking partial designs and block-compatible sequences, §3, explicitly identifies this as the still-open block-design version of Problem 1.1, which retains the size hypothesis: https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/remark191.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: After `answer(sorry) ↔`, restore `∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),` and add `(∀ i, c * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) < ((A i).card : ℝ)) →` before the unique-pair hypothesis. Keep the rest of the conclusion unchanged. Only the restriction `c < 1` is omitted in this variant, not the parameter c or the lower bound on block sizes.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved, §VI, first block-design problem: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf
N. Alon, Blocking partial designs and block-compatible sequences, Problem 1.1, Theorem 2.1, and §3: https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/remark191.pdf

P. Erdős, Some unsolved problems (1997), Cambridge publisher record, DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511662034.004; full text was not accessible: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/3B3C2C2B6FBE588B0E5C36C8598003FF
N. Alon, G. Kalai, J. Matoušek and R. Meshulam, Transversal Numbers for Hypergraphs Arising in Geometry, random half-line construction: https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/akmm6.pdf
review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The main theorem and two_fifths match Alon's Problem 1.1 and Theorem 2.1. The cited external proof and its dependencies compiled successfully; bridge proofs establish both exact repository statements using only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Boundary tests also confirmed that the size hypotheses in these two declarations exclude empty blocks and that 2 / 5 uses real division. No status mismatch was identified in the accessible sources. The live erdosproblems.com/664 page returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive user-agents, so its latest status could not be checked directly; the mathematical comparison used Er81 and Alon's explicit restatement, proof, and concluding remarks. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/linkedproofcheck.lean.

demonstrated.claim: The statement is refuted by n = m = 1 and A 0 = ∅: unique pair coverage holds vacuously, but no set B meets the sole block.

submission.summary: Created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean, refuting the exact imported declaration via type_of%. Compilation succeeds without errors or sorry warnings; the proof uses only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«664»

/-! A one-point counterexample to the block-design variant of Erdős problem 664. -/

-- Erdos664.erdos_664.variants.block_design is false as stated: n = m = 1 and
-- A 0 = ∅ satisfy unique pair coverage vacuously, but no B can meet A 0.
-- The imported `answer(sorry)` slot elaborates to True; we refute its exact type.
theorem block_design_as_stated_is_false :
    ¬ (type_of% @Erdos664.erdos_664.variants.block_design) := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := h.mp True.intro
  obtain ⟨B, hB, _⟩ := hK 1 1 (fun _ => ∅) (by
    intro x y hxy
    exact (hxy (Subsingleton.elim _ _)).elim)
  simpa using hB 0

#print axioms block_design_as_stated_is_false

submission.summary: Restored the positive parameter c and the hypothesis |A_i| > c√n, with K quantified after c so it may depend on c. Clarified the variant's docstring and left all other declarations unchanged. The edited file compiles with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
